rules.title: PostgreSQL 10 is no longer a supported major version
rules.summary: The PostgreSQL Global Development Group lists 10 as unsupported: its final release was on 2022-11-10, so it receives no further bug or security fixes.

constraints: A PostgreSQL data directory written by one major version cannot be started by another. Changing the image tag of a service that has a volume will fail or, worse, start with an empty database.
Upgrade with pg_upgrade or a dump and restore (pg_dumpall, then psql), and move to a supported major in one planned change instead of one major at a time unless the tool you use requires it.
For managed databases, engine_version changes do not apply major upgrades unless allow_major_version_upgrade is set; plan the maintenance window before applying.

steps.title: Back up the data first
steps.instructions: Take a verified backup or snapshot of every PostgreSQL instance in the reported files before changing any version. A major version change is not reversible by changing the version back.

steps.title: Upgrade the database cluster
steps.instructions: Run the upgrade with pg_upgrade or restore a dump into a new instance on the target major version. On a managed database, upgrade through a snapshot restore or a reviewed engine_version change with allow_major_version_upgrade.

steps.title: Raise the declared version
steps.instructions: Change the image tag in Compose files, or engine_version in Terraform, to the release in the replacement. Do this in every file and environment that runs this database, not only the reported line.

steps.title: Check clients and tooling
steps.instructions: Update drivers, ORMs, CI service containers, and local setup documentation that assume the old PostgreSQL version.

verification.purpose: Confirm the Compose file is valid and shows the intended PostgreSQL image tag after the change.
Check that the Terraform configuration is valid with the new engine_version.
Review the plan and confirm the engine_version change is the only database change, and that it is intended.

rules.title: MySQL 5.7 is end-of-life
rules.summary: MySQL 5.7 reached end of life on 2023-10-31 and no longer receives security or bug fixes from Oracle. The mysql.com lifecycle page could not be read when this rule was reviewed (it refuses automated requests), so the date is taken from the endoflife.date record for MySQL.

constraints: MySQL does not support skipping major release lines on upgrade. MySQL 5.7 must move to 8.0 before 8.4; 8.0 can move to 8.4 in place.
A MySQL data directory is upgraded by the new server on first start and cannot be started by the old version again, so a backup is the only way back.
For managed databases, engine_version changes do not apply major upgrades unless allow_major_version_upgrade is set; plan the maintenance window before applying.

steps.title: Back up the data first
steps.instructions: Take a verified backup or snapshot of every MySQL instance in the reported files before changing any version. A major version change is not reversible by changing the version back.

steps.title: Upgrade the database server
steps.instructions: Run mysqlcheck or the MySQL Shell upgrade checker against the old server, fix what it reports, then start the target version on the same data directory, or restore a logical dump into a new instance. On a managed database, upgrade through a snapshot restore or a reviewed engine_version change with allow_major_version_upgrade.

steps.title: Raise the declared version
steps.instructions: Change the image tag in Compose files, or engine_version in Terraform, to the release in the replacement. Do this in every file and environment that runs this database, not only the reported line.

steps.title: Check clients and tooling
steps.instructions: Update drivers, ORMs, CI service containers, and local setup documentation that assume the old MySQL version.

verification.purpose: Confirm the Compose file is valid and shows the intended MySQL image tag after the change.
Check that the Terraform configuration is valid with the new engine_version.
Review the plan and confirm the engine_version change is the only database change, and that it is intended.

rules.title: Azure Database for PostgreSQL 11, 12, and 13 are past standard support
rules.summary: The Azure Database for PostgreSQL version policy lists 2026-07-31 as the standard support end date for PostgreSQL 11, 12, and 13. After that date Azure offers only time-boxed Extended Support, and it does not allow new servers on those major versions.

sources.title: Azure Database for PostgreSQL version policy

constraints: The version argument on azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server and azurerm_postgresql_server names the major version; changing it alone does not move an existing server or its data.
Azure applies a major version upgrade through its managed upgrade operation. Take a backup or point-in-time restore point first, and do not treat changing version back as a rollback.
Azure Extended Support keeps the server running after the standard support end date, but it is time-boxed and does not replace moving to a supported major.

steps.title: Back up the server
steps.instructions: Take a verified backup or point-in-time restore point of every Azure Database for PostgreSQL server reported, before changing its major version.

steps.title: Upgrade the server to a supported major
steps.instructions: Upgrade the server to PostgreSQL 14 or later with Azure's major version upgrade, or restore the backup into a new flexible server on the replacement major and move the application connection string to it.

steps.title: Raise the declared version
steps.instructions: Change version in every azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server and azurerm_postgresql_server block that runs this database, not only the reported line.

steps.title: Check clients and extensions
steps.instructions: Update PostgreSQL drivers, ORMs, extensions, and Azure networking or identity settings that assume the old major version.

verification.purpose: Check that the Terraform configuration is valid with the new version argument.
Review the plan and confirm the version change is intended and is the only server change.
Confirm each reported flexible server now reports a supported PostgreSQL major version.
Confirm any local Compose service that mirrors this database is valid and uses a PostgreSQL image tag that matches the replacement.

rules.title: Azure Database for MySQL 5.7 is past standard support
rules.summary: The Azure Database for MySQL version support policy lists 2026-09-30 as the standard support end date for MySQL 5.7. Azure moves the server to paid Extended Support on 2026-10-01; the MySQL community retired 5.7 on 2023-10-31.

sources.title: Azure Database for MySQL version support policy

constraints: The version argument on azurerm_mysql_flexible_server and azurerm_mysql_server names the major version; changing it alone does not upgrade an existing server or its data.
Upgrade through Azure's managed operation or restore into a new server on the replacement version. A failed upgrade is not reversed by changing version back.
Azure Extended Support keeps MySQL 5.7 running after the standard support end date, but it is time-boxed and may be charged.

steps.title: Back up the server
steps.instructions: Take a verified backup or point-in-time restore point of every Azure Database for MySQL server reported, before changing its version.

steps.title: Upgrade the server to a supported version
steps.instructions: Upgrade the server to MySQL 8.0 or later through Azure's managed upgrade, or restore the backup into a new flexible server on the replacement version and move the application connection string.

steps.title: Raise the declared version
steps.instructions: Change version in every azurerm_mysql_flexible_server and azurerm_mysql_server block that runs this database, not only the reported line.

steps.title: Check clients and authentication
steps.instructions: Update MySQL drivers, ORMs, and users that rely on mysql_native_password; MySQL 8.4 uses caching_sha2_password by default.

verification.purpose: Check that the Terraform configuration is valid with the new version argument.
Review the plan and confirm the version change is intended and is the only server change.
Confirm each reported flexible server now reports a supported MySQL version.
Confirm any local Compose service that mirrors this database is valid and uses a MySQL image tag that matches the replacement.

rules.title: Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL 9.6 through 12 are in extended support
rules.summary: The Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL version policy lists PostgreSQL 9.6, 10, 11, and 12 with extended support starting 2025-02-01 and deprecation on 2028-02-01. The PostgreSQL community no longer supports those majors, and Cloud SQL charges for extended support.

sources.title: Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL database versions and version policies

constraints: Cloud SQL moves an instance to extended support when the PostgreSQL community reaches end of life. Extended support is time-boxed to three years and is charged from 2025-05-01.
Changing database_version can upgrade the instance in place or recreate it, depending on the target. Read the plan before applying and take a backup first.
A major version upgrade cannot be reversed by changing database_version back; restore the backup instead.

steps.title: Back up the instance
steps.instructions: Take an on-demand backup of every Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instance reported, before changing its major version.

steps.title: Upgrade the instance
steps.instructions: Upgrade the instance to PostgreSQL 14 or later with Cloud SQL's in-place major version upgrade, or restore the backup into a new instance on the replacement major and move the application connection string.

steps.title: Raise the declared version
steps.instructions: Change database_version in every google_sql_database_instance and google_sql_source_representation_instance block that runs this database, using the POSTGRES_ prefix for the replacement major.

steps.title: Check clients and extensions
steps.instructions: Update PostgreSQL drivers, ORMs, extensions, and any maintenance or backup automation that names the old major version.

verification.purpose: Check that the Terraform configuration is valid with the new database_version.
Review the plan and confirm the database_version change is intended and is the only instance change.
Confirm each reported instance now reports a supported PostgreSQL database version.
Confirm any local Compose service that mirrors this database is valid and uses a PostgreSQL image tag that matches the replacement.
